item.content:encoded:
State Sen. Nathaniel Ledbetter is calling for a work stoppage on the Escambia County prison project and wants an investigation into construction of a separate prison facility in Elmore County, according to AL.com reporting.

Ledbetter's request signals potential concerns about the Escambia County prison development, though specific details about his objections were not immediately clear. The state senator has also raised questions about the Elmore County prison construction process that he believes warrant formal review.

The Escambia County prison project has been a topic of discussion at the county level as officials work to address capacity and facility needs. Ledbetter's call for investigation and work stoppage could affect the timeline for the local facility's completion.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County has received a FEMA Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance, opening the door for residents to apply for federal aid.

The declaration allows eligible county residents to seek FEMA support for disaster-related damages and losses. Residents can apply for assistance through FEMA's registration process, which typically includes documenting damage, providing proof of residency, and meeting other eligibility requirements.

For more information on how to apply or to check eligibility, residents should visit FEMA's official website or contact their local emergency management office.

The championship represents another feather in the cap for Spanish Fort athletics, adding to the school's growing portfolio of state titles across multiple sports.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Opens Debris Removal Info Line for Storm Cleanup
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is reminding residents that a dedicated Debris Removal Information Line is now open to help with questions about ongoing storm cleanup efforts. The line, available at 833-495-3919, operates seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., according to the county's Communications & Media Relations office. Residents can call to ask about…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is reminding residents that a dedicated Debris Removal Information Line is now open to help with questions about ongoing storm cleanup efforts. The line, available at 833-495-3919, operates seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., according to the county's Communications & Media Relations office.

Residents can call to ask about proper debris placement, pickup schedules, the debris removal process, or to report concerns. The county emphasizes that residents should not contact 911 or Santa Rosa County Emergency Management for debris-related questions — the dedicated info line is the appropriate resource.

The debris collection effort is expected to take several weeks to complete. The county says that proper placement of storm debris helps crews work safely and efficiently, and residents are urged to follow county debris removal guidelines. More information is available at www.santarosa.fl.gov/DebrisInfo.

item.title: Pensacola Hurricane Isaias Public Damage and Recovery Costs Top $47 Million
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The City of Pensacola now estimates Hurricane Isaias caused more than $47 million in damage to public facilities and government recovery costs, while crews continue a debris operation expected to last several more weeks. The latest assessment includes approximately $16 million in projected debris-removal costs.…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The City of Pensacola now estimates Hurricane Isaias caused more than $47 million in damage to public facilities and government recovery costs, while crews continue a debris operation expected to last several more weeks.

The latest assessment includes approximately $16 million in projected debris-removal costs.

Another $24.5 million involves damage to city-owned buildings, parks and other facilities, including Pensacola International Airport, the Port of Pensacola, fire stations and community facilities.

The figure is separate from the city's earlier estimate of more than $71 million in damage to privately owned property.

The new federal Major Disaster Declaration means eligible city expenses can now qualify for FEMA Public Assistance.

Reeves said the federal reimbursement could cover roughly $12 million of the city's projected $16 million debris bill.

Pensacola has collected approximately 347,000 cubic yards of hurricane debris so far.

About two-thirds of city roads have received at least some debris collection, although city officials emphasize that does not mean those streets are finished.

The contractor estimates it will take approximately three more weeks to complete the first full collection pass.

A second pass will begin immediately afterward.

The city has also established a dedicated debris hotline at 833-495-3573 for residents with questions about pickup, eligible debris and how material should be prepared.

The hotline operates from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m., seven days a week.

FEMA Individual Assistance for residents remains under federal review.

item.title: Daylight Saving Time Ends Sunday: AAA Warns of Evening Commute Hazards
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: When clocks fall back an hour early Sunday morning, November 1, drivers across the Panhandle will face shifting visibility challenges that could increase crash risk, according to AAA — The Auto Club Group. The end of daylight saving time means sunset will arrive roughly an hour earlier, pushing more evening commutes into darkness. Research from…
item.content:encoded:
When clocks fall back an hour early Sunday morning, November 1, drivers across the Panhandle will face shifting visibility challenges that could increase crash risk, according to AAA — The Auto Club Group.

The end of daylight saving time means sunset will arrive roughly an hour earlier, pushing more evening commutes into darkness. Research from the AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety shows pedestrian fatalities have climbed dramatically since 2009, with nearly all that increase occurring after dark, particularly on busy city roads. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety also found pedestrian deaths spike when standard time resumes, highlighting the heightened danger for walkers and cyclists in low-light conditions.

"Drivers can expect a noticeable change in their commute almost overnight," said Mark Jenkins, AAA spokesman for The Auto Club Group. "Morning sun glare can make it difficult to see the road ahead, while earlier darkness makes pedestrians and cyclists harder to spot in the evening. Slow down, leave extra space and stay focused, especially around intersections and crosswalks."

AAA recommends checking headlights, taillights, and turn signals before evening drives, keeping sunglasses accessible for morning glare, and reducing speed after dark to stay within the beam of your headlights. The time change also coincides with increased drowsy-driving risk—the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration linked 644 deaths to fatigue-related crashes in 2024. If you feel drowsy behind the wheel, pull over safely to rest rather than push through fatigue.

item.title: Former Pensacola Officer Faces Additional Charges in Ongoing Investigation
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The allegations compound an already troubling case…
item.content:encoded:
A former Pensacola Police Department officer already facing serious charges related to drug possession and child exploitation material has been accused of an additional crime: taking photos of adult men in bathroom stalls without consent, according to arrest documents reviewed by local media.

The allegations compound an already troubling case involving the officer, who was arrested on charges of possessing child sexual abuse material, bestiality videos, and drug paraphernalia. The bathroom surveillance allegations suggest a pattern of behavior investigators are working to fully document.

The Pensacola Police Department and state authorities have not yet released detailed public statements about the scope of the investigation or whether additional charges are expected. The case remains under active review, and investigators may be pursuing further leads.

item.title: Escambia County Legislative Delegation Meets Nov. 12 Before 2027 Session
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Legislative Delegation will host its annual public meeting on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at The Beach Church on Pensacola Beach. The gathering, scheduled from 6:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., comes ahead of the 2027 Florida Legislative Session and gives constituents a chance to weigh in on local priorities. The meeting will be held at…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Legislative Delegation will host its annual public meeting on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at The Beach Church on Pensacola Beach. The gathering, scheduled from 6:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., comes ahead of the 2027 Florida Legislative Session and gives constituents a chance to weigh in on local priorities.

The meeting will be held at The Beach Church, 920 Panferio Drive on Pensacola Beach. According to North Escambia reporting, the annual forum allows community members to present issues and concerns to the delegation before lawmakers head to Tallahassee for the next legislative session.

The delegation typically uses these public meetings to gather feedback on education, infrastructure, public safety, and other matters affecting Escambia County before introducing bills and priorities at the state level.

item.content:encoded:
The Tate High School FFA Chapter has captured first place in the Florida Turfgrass Science Invitational Student Competition, held at Candler Hills Golf Course at On Top of the World in Ocala. The win advances the team to nationals competition.

The championship team included Baylor Touchstone, Addyson Smallwood, Allison Wynne, and Cade McNair. The competition tests students' knowledge and skills in turfgrass management and science across a range of practical and theoretical challenges.

This marks another state title for the Tate High FFA program, which continues to establish itself as a competitive force in agricultural education across Escambia County.

item.title: Escambia Children's Trust allocates $3.6M annually to youth programs, including Century hub
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Children's Trust board this week approved $3.6 million in yearly funding for community youth and family programs across the county, including more than $1 million over three years for a new learning and readiness hub in Century. The Extra Mile Club Str8 Up will receive $349,650 annually—totaling $1,048,950 over three years—to…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Children's Trust board this week approved $3.6 million in yearly funding for community youth and family programs across the county, including more than $1 million over three years for a new learning and readiness hub in Century.

The Extra Mile Club Str8 Up will receive $349,650 annually—totaling $1,048,950 over three years—to operate the "Soul Train Little Learners & Family Readiness Hub" in Century. The hub is designed to serve early learners and families in the North Escambia area.

The broader funding package, approved this week, directs more than $3.6 million per year to various youth-focused initiatives across Escambia County. The Children's Trust, a county agency, oversees investments in early childhood development, after-school programs, family support services, and related community initiatives.

item.content:encoded:
Downtown Pensacola's Palafox Market is going all-out for Halloween this Saturday, with a lineup of family-friendly activities running from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Plaza Ferdinand & MLK Jr. Plaza.

Attendees can expect a Creepy Crawly Zoo, mini-train rides, a Haunted Trolley, trick-or-treating, and other seasonal attractions. The market, which operates every Saturday, is transforming into a festive Halloween destination for the community.

If you're looking for a way to celebrate the holiday in Pensacola, the Halloween-themed Palafox Market offers activities for all ages without having to venture far from downtown.
